finding.claim: UpyunCallbackAuth writes a 401 on signature-validation failure but does not abort, so the upload callback still runs and completes the upload session. Signature verification is cosmetic for Upyun callbacks.
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST to /api/v4/callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key with a forged body. Precondition: attacker knows a valid sessionID/key pair (own upload session or leaked key).
finding.sink: ProcessCallback -> callback.ProcessCallback(c) (routers/controllers/callback.go:19) finalises the upload session using attacker-supplied callback body.

trace.note: Route callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key: UseUploadSession -> UpyunCallbackAuth -> ProcessCallback
upyun.ValidateCallback returns error; result is only used for logging
401 JSON written, no c.Abort() or return
c.Next() runs unconditionally, so the handler chain continues
ProcessCallback runs and completes the session

finding.guards_checked: UseUploadSession (session lookup by sessionID/key; code not in repo, assumed to check key). upyun.ValidateCallback (signature; result discarded). No other gate on this path.

finding.claim: Direct-link create (PUT) and delete (DELETE) under file/source inherit only RequiredScopes(FilesRead) and do not require FilesWrite, unlike every other write route in the file group.
finding.source: Bearer/OAuth token granted files.read scope only.
finding.sink: explorer.GetDirectLinkService (creates a public share link to a file) via controllers/file.go:116-134; DeleteDirectLink via controllers/file.go:136-144.

trace.note: file.Use(RequiredScopes(ScopeFilesRead)) applied to the whole file group
source := file.Group("source") inherits the read-only scope middleware
source.PUT("") has no RequiredScopes(ScopeFilesWrite)
source.DELETE(":id") has no RequiredScopes(ScopeFilesWrite)

finding.guards_checked: Session/CurrentUser middleware; RequiredScopes(FilesRead) only. Semantics of RequiredScopes live in middleware/, not in repo; verify before reporting.

finding.claim: Any logged-in user can submit an arbitrary URL that the server fetches (remote download), with no URL or IP validation visible in the controller layer.
finding.sink: Server-side HTTP fetch inside explorer.DownloadWorkflowService.CreateDownloadTask (code not in repo).

trace.note: wf group: LoginRequired
remoteDownload.POST("") with RequiredScopes(WorkflowWrite)
CreateRemoteDownload parses FromJSON DownloadWorkflowService and calls CreateDownloadTask

finding.guards_checked: LoginRequired, RequiredScopes(WorkflowWrite). No URL allowlist, scheme check, or private-IP check in the controller layer. Connect-time IP enforcement must be verified in the service (case 12).

finding.claim: Share and workflow-task mutations pass a client-supplied hashid straight into service calls with no owner argument; ownership enforcement is unverifiable from this code (IDOR candidate across several routes).
finding.source: Authenticated user supplies another user's share/task/direct-link/upload-session/WebDAV/passkey ID in the URL or body.
finding.sink: share.DeleteShare(c, id), share.BatchDeleteShare, EditShare Upsert (controllers/share.go:24-26, 65-66, 75-80); workflow.go:27-29, 45-48, 58-60; file.go:136-137; file.go:232-243; webdav.go:41-44, 57-58; user.go:63-66.

trace.note: share routes apply HashID(ShareID) and pass context to controller
hashid.FromContext(c) passed to share.DeleteShare with no caller identity
direct-link delete: HashID(SourceLinkID) then DeleteDirectLink
GetTaskPhaseProgress(c, taskId): taskId from HashID only

finding.guards_checked: HashID middleware (decodes only), LoginRequired and RequiredScopes at route level. No owner or tenant scoping visible in controllers. Owner checks must be verified in service/ (cases 05, 09).

finding.claim: Several upload-callback routes (onedrive, cos, s3, ks3, obs) have no signature or auth validator; the only gate is UseUploadSession, so anyone who can construct sessionID/key may finalise uploads.
finding.sink: ProcessCallback -> callback.ProcessCallback(c) finalises the upload session.

trace.note: onedrive POST: UseUploadSession then ProcessCallback, no validator
cos GET: UseUploadSession then ProcessCallback, no validator
s3 GET: UseUploadSession then ProcessCallback, no validator
ks3 GET: UseUploadSession then ProcessCallback, no validator
obs POST: UseUploadSession then ProcessCallback, no validator

finding.guards_checked: UseUploadSession only (not in repo). Compare with OSSCallbackAuth, QiniuCallbackValidate, RemoteCallbackAuth, UpyunCallbackAuth, which are present on other providers.

finding.claim: WOPI endpoints take the file ID from the URL, and ViewerSessionValidation may not bind the viewer session to that file, so a session for file A may read or write file B.
finding.source: Holder of a valid WOPI viewer session for file A requests /api/v4/file/wopi/:id with id of file B.
finding.sink: CheckFileInfo/GetFile/PutFile/ModifyFile (routers/controllers/wopi.go:12-82) operate on the file resolved from :id.

trace.note: wopi group: HashID(FileID) and ViewerSessionValidation()
wopi.GET(":id") -> CheckFileInfo
wopi.POST(":id/contents") -> PutFile
CheckFileInfo uses zero-value explorer.WopiService; file resolved from context

finding.guards_checked: HashID decoding; ViewerSessionValidation (code not in repo). Whether it compares session file to :id is unknown.

finding.claim: Archive extraction may write entries outside the destination if entry names are not sanitised (zip-slip); the extraction code is not in the repo.
finding.source: Logged-in user with workflows.write uploads or references an archive containing ../ entry names.
finding.sink: ArchiveWorkflowService.CreateExtractTask (routers/controllers/file.go:86-101) writes extracted entries to a destination path.

ExtractArchive -> service.CreateExtractTask

finding.guards_checked: LoginRequired, RequiredScopes(WorkflowWrite). Path sanitisation of entry names is not visible; verify in the service (case 20).

finding.claim: The 2FA OTP endpoint has no rate-limit or captcha middleware, so a 6-digit OTP may be brute-forced unless the service enforces an attempt limit.
finding.source: Attacker who has a valid twoFaSession (after password login) posts guessed OTP codes to /api/v4/session/token/2fa.
finding.sink: Verify2FA (routers/controllers/user.go:97-108) accepts or rejects the OTP and issues a token via UserIssueToken.

trace.note: token.POST("2fa") has no rate-limit or captcha middleware
CaptchaRequired applies only to the login route, not 2FA
UserLogin2FAValidation -> service.Verify2FA

finding.guards_checked: Captcha on login only; no attempt-counting visible. Attempt limit inside Verify2FA not in repo.
